A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable main text, equations, figures and appendices. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Section 5 and Figures 2–6 report original attack experiments on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and adds original norm-constraint and ImageNet results in Appendix D, Tables 1–3.

M1.justification: Appendix D.3 introduces sparse Softmax cross-entropy fine-tuning of VGG16, Inception-V3 and Visformer before ensemble attacks, producing MI-FGSM-S, SVRE-S and SIA-S. This is a concrete training-objective adaptation; the earlier attack procedures remain.

E1.justification: v3 adds ImageNet evaluation, substantially extending the earlier small-image benchmark coverage. MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 remain; CIFAR-100 moves from v2 Appendix E to v3 Appendix D.1.

E2.justification: The earlier experiments use MI-FGSM without the corresponding SVRE or SIA comparisons. Table 3 introduces direct comparisons between MI-FGSM, SVRE and SIA and their sparse-loss variants, substantially expanding the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: New experimental designs include six max-norm thresholds across six network configurations and original-versus-sparse surrogate comparisons across eight ImageNet target architectures. The previously reported training settings and 20-step MI-FGSM evaluations remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D.2 adds a direct sensitivity study of norm constraints and attack effectiveness. Appendix D.3 tests whether sparse fine-tuning changes weight norms and attack performance. These add substantial evidence about complexity control beyond the retained step-count, ensemble-size and weight-decay analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The retained prediction-variance plots measure ensemble diversity, rather than statistical uncertainty; the new tables introduce no uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 add accuracy, weight-norm and ImageNet attack results. Table 3 reports MI-FGSM/MI-FGSM-S scores of 66.0/68.9 on ResNet50, but SIA/SIA-S scores of 98.4/98.2 on MobileNetV2, showing gains are not universal. Existing results in Figures 2–6 are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix C.6 adds independent and dependent Hellinger-term derivations with assumptions about an influential subset of models. The retained model-space extension, Theorem D.1 becoming C.6, changes its coefficient under the square root from 2γβ²/N to 18γβ²/N and changes the logarithmic constant. v2's X-divergence definition and domain-adaptation bound in D.4.2 are removed; the main theorems remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central definitions, vulnerability-diversity decomposition, transferability bound and guidelines concerning ensemble size, diversity and complexity. The new experiments support these existing contribution claims.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the new experiments through loss of model capacity under tight norm constraints and the benefits of sparse fine-tuning. Appendix C.6 adds conditional discussion of how the dependency term scales with ensemble size and identifies estimating the influential model subset as an open problem. The domain-alignment interpretation in v2 D.4.2 is removed.

D1.justification: v3 documents max-norm thresholds, per-weight-vector L2 constraints, ImageNet surrogate backbones and the sparse fine-tuning loss. These provide technical information for the new experiments, although their fine-tuning budgets and complete attack settings remain unspecified. Earlier implementation disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds discussion of Fan et al. on transferability and flatness, Chen et al. on bias-variance alignment, and references supporting the new experiments and Hellinger analysis. It removes domain-adaptation references and associated novelty positioning. The extended related-work appendix is otherwise retained after relocation.

P1.justification: The appendices are substantially reorganized, with related work moved first, theory extensions grouped with proofs, and experiments collected separately. The contents pages are removed, the extended analogy discussion moves into Section 4.3, several discussion lists become prose, and publication and acknowledgement text is added.

P2.justification: v3 adds three compact experimental tables, enlarges Figure 1 and relocates Figures 5 and 6. All six existing figure graphics are retained; the remaining visual changes principally involve placement, spacing and mathematical display layout.

improvement.justification: The norm-control and ImageNet comparisons provide more direct support for the practical complexity guideline, and the retained extension's constants now agree with Theorem 4.3. These gains are limited by incomplete new protocol details, removal of the domain-adaptation treatment, and a local algebraic error in C.6: its displayed 1+(beta1^-1-1)/(1-beta1) equals 1+beta1^-1, rather than being at most beta1^-1.
